Fats

Fats — types, sources, functions, essential fatty acids and role in health.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Classify fats and name examples
  • Describe the functions of fats
  • Explain essential fatty acids and cholesterol

In simple words

Fats are a concentrated source of energy. One gram of fat gives about 9 kcal — more than twice that of carbohydrates or protein. Fats also form cell membranes, carry fat-soluble vitamins and make hormones.

Fats are classified as saturated, unsaturated and trans fats. Saturated and trans fats raise heart disease risk; unsaturated fats are healthier.

Types of fats

Type Examples Health effect
Saturated Ghee, butter, coconut oil, red meat Raise blood cholesterol
Unsaturated Vegetable oils, fish, nuts Generally healthier
Trans Vanaspati, fried snacks, baked goods Worst for heart health

Functions

  • Concentrated energy (9 kcal per gram).
  • Form cell membranes and nerve sheaths.
  • Carry fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K.
  • Make hormones.
  • Insulate and protect organs.

Essential fatty acids

Linoleic acid and alpha-linolenic acid cannot be made by the body and must come from food (vegetable oils, fish, nuts).

Daily requirement

About 20–30% of total daily energy should come from fats, mostly unsaturated. Saturated fat should be less than 10% of energy.

🔴 Energy value of fat

One gram of fat gives about 9 kcal. Fats should give 20–30% of daily energy, mostly unsaturated; saturated fat below 10%.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Heart-healthy diet — advise less ghee, butter and fried food; more vegetable oils, fish and nuts.
  • Weight management — fat is energy-dense; excess leads to obesity.
  • Fat-soluble vitamins — vitamins A, D, E and K need fat for absorption.
  • Patient teaching — explain that not all fat is bad; choose unsaturated over saturated and trans fats.
  • Cholesterol — high blood cholesterol raises heart disease risk; counsel on diet and medication.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Fats are a concentrated energy source: 1 g = about 9 kcal.
  2. Types: saturated, unsaturated and trans fats.
  3. Saturated and trans fats raise heart disease risk; unsaturated fats are healthier.
  4. Fats carry fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K.
  5. 20–30% of daily energy should come from fats.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Essential fatty acids (linoleic, alpha-linolenic) must come from food.
  2. Fats form cell membranes and nerve sheaths and make hormones.
  3. Vanaspati and fried snacks contain trans fats — avoid.
  4. Saturated fat should be below 10% of daily energy.

📌 Memory trick

Fat types: “SUT” — Saturated (bad), Unsaturated (better), Trans (worst).

60-second revision

  • Fats = concentrated energy; 1 g = 9 kcal.
  • Saturated (bad), Unsaturated (better), Trans (worst).
  • Carry vitamins A, D, E, K; make hormones.
  • 20-30% of daily energy from fat; saturated below 10%.
  • Essential fatty acids from food.

Test yourself

One gram of fat gives about:

Answer: C. One gram of fat provides about 9 kilocalories.

Which fat is worst for heart health?

Answer: C. Trans fats are the worst for heart health.

Fats should provide about what percent of daily energy?

Answer: B. About 20–30% of total daily energy should come from fats.

Essential fatty acids:

Answer: B. Essential fatty acids cannot be made by the body and must come from food.

Which food contains saturated fat?

Answer: B. Ghee is rich in saturated fat.
